column3: Quillstack 4.2 adds offline editing, a faster search index and a new permissions model for shared spaces. Most installations can upgrade in place without downtime.
Pages you have opened in the last 30 days stay editable when the connection drops. Changes are kept as drafts and merged when you are back online.
Offline drafts are stored in the browser and synchronised on reconnect.
Tables can now be pasted from spreadsheets with their formatting kept.
The index is rebuilt incrementally, which cuts reindexing time by about 70%.
Results can be filtered by space and by author.
Space owners can delegate permissions to groups.
The audit log can be exported as CSV.
The configuration key search.engine has been renamed to search.backend.
Support for PostgreSQL 13 has been removed; use version 14 or later.
The legacy endpoint /api/v1/export now returns 410 Gone.
Back up the database and the attachments folder before you upgrade. The commands below assume a Debian-based server.
$ quillstack backup --output /var/backups/qs-$(date +%F).tar.gz $ sudo systemctl stop quillstack $ sudo apt install quillstack=4.2.0-1 $ quillstack migrate --check $ sudo systemctl start quillstack
After upgrading, update quillstack.yaml as shown below.
search: backend: tantivy index _ rebuild: incremental offline: enabled: true max _ draft _ age _ days: 30 permissions: delegate _ to _ groups: true

Version 4.2.1 is planned for the second half of November. Report problems through the support portal.
